selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The Northern Montana Water Security Act of 2025 ratifies a water rights settlement agreement between the United States, Montana, and the Fort Belknap Indian Community (representing the Gros Ventre and Assiniboine Tribes). It places the community's water rights in trust, mandates the creation of a tribal water code, authorizes land exchanges and transfers to be held in trust (with gaming prohibited), establishes trust and implementation funds with both authorized and mandatory appropriations, and provides funding for wastewater infrastructure on the Blackfeet Indian Reservation.

affected_groups.effect: Receives recognized and ratified tribal water rights held in trust, water allocations from Lake Elwell, funding for irrigation, water, and sewer systems, trust funds, land transfers into reservation status, and cancels debts or liens related to construction assessments and operation/maintenance charges for the irrigation project.
affected_groups.group: Fort Belknap Indian Community (Gros Ventre and Assiniboine Tribes) and members

affected_groups.effect: Water rights and interests are held in trust by the United States, entitled to a just and equitable allocation of water for irrigation, and benefit from the elimination of certain debts and liens against their allotments.
affected_groups.group: Allottees of the Fort Belknap Reservation

affected_groups.effect: Participates in water rights compact execution, land exchange negotiations with federal agencies, and contributes a $5,000,000 cost share upon Montana Water Court final decree approval.

Receives authorization of appropriations up to $250,000,000 for planning, designing, constructing, operating, maintaining, and replacing community water distribution and wastewater treatment facilities.

key_provisions: Modifies and ratifies a specified water rights settlement agreement (Compact) for the Fort Belknap Indian Community and allottees.
Requires the Fort Belknap Indian Community to enact a tribal water code and hold its water rights in trust without risk of loss through non-use, forfeiture, or abandonment.

Authorizes the Department of the Interior and Department of Agriculture to negotiate state-for-federal land exchanges to be placed into trust for the community, and transfers specified federal and tribal fee lands into trust while prohibiting gaming on all trust land taken under the bill.
Allocates 20,000 acre-feet per year of water stored in Lake Elwell to the Fort Belknap Indian Community.
Authorizes the Secretary to carry out restoration of the St. Mary Canal and enlargement of the Dodson South Canal for Milk River Project mitigation, backed by up to $300,000,000 in obligations.
Authorizes up to $415,832,153 for the Secretary to rehabilitate, modernize, and expand the Fort Belknap Indian Irrigation Project.

Establishes the Aaniiih Nakoda Settlement Trust Fund and the Fort Belknap Indian Community Water Settlement Implementation Fund with specific accounts, funded through both authorized appropriations and mandatory appropriations.
Authorizes $250,000,000 to be appropriated to the Secretary of the Interior for community water distribution and wastewater treatment facilities for the Blackfeet Tribe.

It places the community's water rights in trust, mandates the creation of a tribal water code, authorizes land exchanges and transfers to be held in trust (with gaming prohibited), establishes trust and implementation funds with both authorized and mandatory appropriations, and provides funding for wastewater infrastructure on the Blackfeet Indian Reservation.
summary_detail.significance: The bill represents a major statutory settlement of Indian water rights and infrastructure funding in Montana, involving hundreds of millions of dollars in mandatory and authorized appropriations, extensive land transfers into federal trust, and large-scale water project construction and mitigation efforts.
